I just started using Lean with emacs. I have a couple questions, since I've had a lot of friction so far. I really don't want to use VS code:

Is there an authoritative emacs mode? I've seen stuff about nael, lean4-mode, as well as a bunch of forks. Which should I actually use? I've mostly tried out things with the official lean4-mode git repository

How do I get indentation to work correctly?

Is completion really slow for anyone else? I had to change the lsp-timeout with lean4 mode way up, and in an empty file which just uses Mathlib, doing Nat.mul_ <C-M-i> takes 10 seconds or so. Surely everyone is having instant comletion suggestions from the way MIL says to explore this way. And does anyone have a good set up for showing documentation of the function when going over a completion candidate with company (or anything else, I'm not sure what works best)

I just started using Lean with emacs. I have a couple questions, since I've had a lot of friction so far. I really don't want to use VS code:

Great; sorry to hear that; nah, me neither.

Is there an authoritative emacs mode? I've seen stuff about nael, lean4-mode, as well as a bunch of forks. Which should I actually use? I've mostly tried out things with the official lean4-mode git repository

I have nothing to say about leanprover-community/lean4-mode. I'd certainly recommend trying Nael. I haven't actually tried @Lua Viana Reis's lean-ts-mode but I'm prepared to bet it's excellent. Mine and @Paul Nelson's lean4-mode forks (which are usually similar if not identical, at least up until now) seem to work ok (let us know if not); if you customize lean4-info-plain to nil you'll get Paul's excellent "hover docs" feature which annotates terms in the infoview with their type, which I find indispensible. There may be others I don't know about.

How do I get indentation to work correctly?

It doesn't work well in the official lean4-mode, or in my fork (Paul might be looking into a rewrite); I have got used to the frustration of indenting manually. It might be better in Nael, or in Lua's fork.

Is completion really slow for anyone else? I had to change the lsp-timeout with lean4 mode way up, and in an empty file which just uses Mathlib, doing Nat.mul_ <C-M-i> takes 10 seconds or so. Surely everyone is having instant comletion suggestions from the way MIL says to explore this way.

The candidates are generated by the language server (Lean), so I don't think Emacs is much slower than VSCode. Lean has a lot to search through, especially if the whole of Mathlib is imported. I think people just get used to being patient. You can import a smaller set of modules to get faster completion, but you risk missing out on candidates that are defined outside that set of modules.

And does anyone have a good set up for showing documentation of the function when going over a completion candidate with company (or anything else, I'm not sure what works best)

Sounds nice! But I don't know about anything like that. (I use Company.)

@Richard Copley that's a really useful summary - I found myself pushed towards using VS Code for Lean only where I feel so much less productive than in emacs. I am going to go through your suggestions and see if I can get an acceptable Lean / emacs.

Richard covered everything well. Here's my fork, which is typically in sync with his.

Happy to share my experimental lean4-indent-line function (still a bit too embarrassing to put online, DM me if you're interested)

Thank you @Richard Copley for the detailed answer. I tried nael and the forks. I wasn't able to figure out how to get documentation tooltips on mouse-over working as well on eglot as lsp-mode though, so I suppose I'll stick with lsp-mode for the time being. Nael also just crashed with an infinite lisp nesting error when I tried it with lsp-mode. The performance is mostly the huge issue for me so far, where opening a file from MIL can take up to a minute in emacs with little feedback from the different lean-modes. But I guess this is must be an issue on VS code as well?

Maybe the next step is to fix the language server's performance...

In any case, I may try to work on profiling and optimizing both the lean language server and work on the emacs modes once I get familiar enough with lean. If I understand correctly, it's not the resolution I would have liked: they should just do the calculation correctly for the default mode. It is very cheap, as demonstrated by Eglot. Anyway, if the Lean server supports the mode to thich the resolution applies, maybe the problem is effectively solved. See how you get on!

Thank you for this thread that motivated me to try to come back to Emacs when using Lean. I'm trying out the lean4-mode fork of Paul Nelson. There are a few roadblocks, for which you may have workarounds. I'm posting them here, but it might also make for a new thread:

  1. No syntax highlighting in the Lean Goal buffer
  2. No way to jump to definitions of terms in the Lean Goal buffer
  3. I found the ability to hover on terms/sub-terms in the vscode info view very handy. Eldoc-mouse do not give me the same, as I'm not able to hover on "a region" (usefull when there are notations)
  4. How do you get the buffers organized between Lean Goal and eldoc ?

I am used to 1, 2 and 3. I've just tried eldoc-mouse for the first time in the Lean Goal buffer, and I agree it doesn't seem to work as well as one might hope. You might be surprised how easy it is to put point in the right place in the Lean Goal buffer to get the annotation for the exact subexpression you're looking for (on whitespace, parentheses, operators, identifiers). Remember to customize lean4-info-plain to nil.

For 4, I have the below in my init.el. It's quite specific to my personal preferences. I didn't put any effort into making it customizable. When I want to see both Lean Goal and eldoc I just do that manually; if I find myself doing it a lot, I sometimes remember to save the window configuration to a register.

(declare-function lean4-ensure-info-buffer "lean4-info")
(defvar lean4-mode-map)

(defun help!-lean (&optional interactive)
  "If neither `*Lean Goal*' nor `*eldoc' is visible, reorganise the window
and show `*Lean Goal*`. If both are visible, do nothing. If one is visible,
switch it to the other."
  (interactive '(t))
  (when (and (eq major-mode 'lean4-mode)
             (buffer-file-name))
    (let* ((goals-buf (get-buffer "*Lean Goal*"))
           (goals-win (and (buffer-live-p goals-buf)
                           (get-buffer-window goals-buf 'visible)))
           (eldoc-buf (get-buffer "*eldoc*"))
           (eldoc-win (and (buffer-live-p eldoc-buf)
                           (get-buffer-window eldoc-buf 'visible)))
           buf win)
      (cond ((not goals-win)
             (lean4-ensure-info-buffer "*Lean Goal*")
             (setq buf (setq goals-buf (get-buffer "*Lean Goal*"))
                   win eldoc-win))
            ((not eldoc-win)
             (unless (buffer-live-p eldoc-buf)
               (let ((display-buffer-overriding-action
                      '(display-buffer-no-window allow-no-window t)))
                 (eldoc interactive))
               (setq eldoc-buf (get-buffer "*eldoc*")))
             (setq buf eldoc-buf
                   win goals-win)))
      (when buf
        (unless win
          (delete-other-windows)
          (setq win (split-window-horizontally)))
        (set-window-buffer win buf)))))

(with-eval-after-load 'lean4-mode
  (define-key lean4-mode-map [f1] #'help!-lean))

@Clément Blaudeau The community version of lean4 does have 3) with lsp-ui-doc, not in the info view, but with great hover support for expressions. This is actually what kept me using the community version. It would be great to have this feature in the eldoc version. With eldoc-mouse, I almost now have something similar, but highlighting the expression on the parenthesis in e.g. (f hx) does not show the type of the whole expression, though it does show it in the eldoc. It would be great to fix this.

I've made an issue for this: https://github.com/huangfeiyu/eldoc-mouse/issues/27

I wonder if the goal buffer could automatically have nice things like <-. and syntax highlighting as well as hover docs if the goal buffer were able to inherit the eglot-managed-mode of the lean buffer it is be an infoview of.
